cells.tense: Present — here, with the pen in hand.
cells.verb: choosing to join with something and letting the two of you become one current
cells.place: in the place where you look after what's still growing
cells.ask: let the closeness you've chosen pick a direction, and hold that direction the next time something leans against it — because when this is working, the dreaming comes from having actually lived the thing, not from wishing at it.
cells.core:
You've chosen to be in this with what you're tending — not standing over it, not watching from the door, but in it. The care isn't a job you perform at it; you and the growing thing are moving together, and you can tell the difference between that and simply hovering. That's a real choice, made once and kept.

What this is free to feed next: direction. Closeness like this knows where it wants to go. Let it say so, and keep saying so when something pushes back.
cells.sheetLine: You've chosen to be in this with what you're growing, and the choosing is yours.

cells.tense: Future — braced against a tomorrow that hasn't been written yet.
cells.verb: pouring yourself so far into what you're tending that there's no seam left between you and it
cells.place: in the place where you look after what's still growing
cells.ask: pick one thing you're tending and let it be, for a day, without your hands on it — and notice what it has already become on its own. That's what the care was for: a dream that comes from having fully digested what happened, not one that runs ahead of it.
cells.core:
You've joined with what you're growing so completely that you're living its future for it. Every stage it hasn't reached yet, you've already felt — and so you're tending ahead of its timing, filling in what hasn't happened, bracing for weather that isn't here. The closeness is real. It has just stopped leaving room for the thing to arrive on its own.

The way back is not less care. It's letting the care rest long enough to see what it already produced.
cells.sheetLine: You're so far inside what you're growing that you've started growing it for it.

cells.tense: Past — still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: holding back from joining with what you're tending, keeping one foot outside the current
cells.place: in the place where you look after what's still growing
cells.ask: say one thing you already perceive about what you're tending — plainly, without defending it, and without needing to be sure. Let your own knowing do the work your closeness isn't doing yet. That's where the dreaming comes back from: from having let what happened be finished.
cells.core:
You're looking after this at arm's length. The care is happening — the watering, the attention — but you haven't stepped into the current with it, and some part of you is still standing at an earlier door where stepping in didn't go well. The thing is growing. You're just not quite in the room with it.

The way through isn't to force yourself closer. It's to trust what you can already see about it, and let that pull you in.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending it from the doorway, not from inside.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down in a room you're already writing.
cells.verb: already flowing as one with what you're tending, while calling it simply looking after
cells.place: in the place where you look after what's still growing
cells.ask: name, once and out loud, the direction you've been quietly steering this toward — as yours, not as what it 'needed'. Say it the way you'd point out a path to someone: plainly, without force. Then the dream has an author again, and it comes from everything you've actually lived with it.
cells.core:
You're already joined with this. It shapes how you move, what you give it, what you let go; people can see that you and it are one thing by now. But you'd describe yourself as just taking care of it, as if the care were running itself and you happened to be nearby. The joining happened. The owning of it hasn't.

What's missing is simple: saying which way you're pointing it, in your own voice.
cells.sheetLine: You've already become one with what you're growing. You still call it minding it.
